name: Kykuit
unique: The Rockefeller estate above the Hudson with a six story view, a basement full of Picasso tapestries and Chinese ceramics, and a terraced garden by William Welles Bosworth.
buzz: The art tour is worth the extra ticket over the classic house tour; the coach from the visitor center is mandatory and the whole thing runs like a museum.

name: Playland Park
customer: Coaster people, families, art deco fans
unique: The oldest continuously operating amusement park in the country, an art deco seaside complex where the 1929 Dragon Coaster still runs through a wooden dragon mouth.
buzz: Coaster people come for the Dragon and the historical buildings; the ride lineup is small and the westchester beach next door is the calm alternative.

name: Untermyer Gardens
unique: A walled Persian garden and a rock and water feature built for a Gilded Age lawyer, largely forgotten for decades and now restored above the Hudson in Yonkers.
buzz: The walled garden is the reveal, and the view down to the Palisades is the second one; volunteers run free weekend tours.

name: Bear Mountain State Park
unique: The wooded hill above the Hudson where the Appalachian Trail crosses a zoo of native animals, a 1920s lodge and a stone tower with a view over the river bends.
buzz: The Perkins Tower drive is the easy win, the Major Welch trail is the real hike, and the lot fills by ten on fall weekends.

name: Edward Hopper House
unique: The clapboard house where Hopper was born and painted the light he spent his life chasing, with his easel and a garden that faces the same south light.
buzz: Small and personal, and the reason to come is seeing the rooms that appear in the paintings; the upstairs gallery shows young artists.

name: Hook Mountain
unique: A short climb to a traprock ridge above the Tappan Zee where turkey vultures ride the updraft and the Palisades sit across the water like a wall.
buzz: The loop from Rockland Lake is the standard route; the ridge is narrow with real drop offs and the parking lot is tiny on weekends.

name: Manitoga
customer: Design people, mid century fans, gardeners
unique: Industrial designer Russel Wright's house built into a quarry and a woodland garden he planted by hand, with a moss floor and a pool that reflects the hemlocks.
buzz: The house tour is the only way in and it is limited; designers leave talking about the window that frames a single tree.

name: Boscobel House and Gardens
customer: House tour people, gardeners, theater goers
unique: A Federal mansion moved brick by brick in the 1950s to a bluff above the Hudson, with period furniture and a rose garden that faces West Point across the river.
buzz: The view from the lawn is the best on the Hudson; the summer Shakespeare festival on the grounds is the local tradition.

name: Breakneck Ridge
customer: Hikers, trail runners, city day trippers
unique: A rock scramble straight up the Hudson Highlands from a train station platform, three false summits and a ridge walk with the river 900 feet below.
buzz: It is the most crowded hike in the region for a reason; go before eight, wear real shoes, and skip it when the rocks are wet.

name: Motorcyclepedia Museum
unique: Eighty five thousand square feet of motorcycles including a wall of police bikes, a circular room of Indians and a 1908 Harley, put together by a collector who never sold one.
buzz: People arrive expecting a small collection and stay three hours; the police motorcycle room is the surprise.

name: Brotherhood Winery
unique: The oldest continuously operating winery in the country, with tours through brick cellars dug by hand in the 1830s and a tasting room in the old press house.
buzz: The cellar tour is the reason to go; the wine is not why oenophiles come back and the holiday events fill the place.

name: Harriman State Park
unique: Forty seven thousand acres of lakes and ridge line where Seven Lakes Drive winds past swimming beaches, a stone tower and the remains of colonial iron works.
buzz: Lake Sebago is the swim, Anthony Wayne is the easy hike, and locals guard the quieter lakes; the park is bigger than the map suggests.

name: Walkway Over the Hudson
unique: A ruined 1889 railroad bridge rebuilt as a 1.28 mile pedestrian deck 212 feet above the Hudson, with a glass elevator down to the river trail.
buzz: Sunset is the time, the wind is constant, and the elevator on the Poughkeepsie side saves the stairs; it is fully accessible.

name: Home of Franklin D. Roosevelt
unique: Springwood, the Hudson river house where Roosevelt was born and ran a presidency, with his desk, his ship models and the grave where he and Eleanor are buried in the rose garden.
buzz: The house tour and the library are separate tickets; the grounds and the Valkill cottage next door are the quiet part most people miss.

name: Culinary Institute of America
customer: Food people, couples, parents visiting students
unique: Four student run restaurants where the people cooking your lunch are weeks away from graduating, on a campus that was a Jesuit seminary above the Hudson.
buzz: Reservations are essential for the American Bounty and Bocuse rooms; the prix fixe lunch is the bargain and the bread basket is famous.

name: Mohonk Mountain House
unique: A Victorian castle on a cliff above a glacial lake, with 85 miles of carriage roads, a rock scramble called the Labyrinth and a lemonade porch that has served guests since Grant.
buzz: Day passes need booking and are not cheap; the Labyrinth and Eagle Cliff are the hike, and the porch is worth a slow hour.

name: Shawangunk Ridge Climbing
unique: The Gunks: a quartz conglomerate cliff line with horizontal cracks so friendly that beginners lead their first routes here, plus carriage roads and a raptor migration in fall.
buzz: Guides say it is the best place in the east to learn to trad climb; the carriage roads are the backup when the cliffs are crowded.

name: Opus 40
unique: A six and a half acre bluestone sculpture built by one man over 37 years in a quarry he bought for the stone, with ramps and pools that you are allowed to walk on.
buzz: People call it the best unknown place in the Catskills; the founder fell to his death at the site and is buried under the sculpture.

name: Hudson River Maritime Museum
unique: A waterfront museum with a 1890s wooden tug, a working boat shop and the story of the ice harvest and brick barges that built the river economy.
buzz: Small and well made, and the lighthouse cruise and the tug are the reasons to check the schedule before driving over.

name: New York State Museum
customer: Families, history people, rainy day crowds
unique: A free state museum with a mastodon pulled from a Orange County bog, a full sized Adirondack lean to, and the largest collection of World Trade Center artifacts in the country.
buzz: The September 11 gallery is the reason many people come; the carousel and the mineral room keep children moving.

name: USS Slater
unique: The last destroyer escort still afloat, a 1944 ship built in Tampa that crossed the Atlantic and now sits in the Port of Albany with its guns, depth charges and crew quarters intact.
buzz: The volunteer guides are frequently former navy and will talk for an hour; the ship is tight and steep and not for strollers.

name: New York State Capitol Tour
company: New York State Office of General Services
customer: Architecture people, school groups, statehouse collectors
unique: A capitol built over 32 years without a dome, with a carved stone staircase that climbs four floors without support and a hall of governors that looks like a cathedral.
buzz: The Million Dollar Staircase is the thing to see; tours are free and run on the hour, and the observation deck is open in summer.

name: Troy Waterfront Farmers Market
unique: A year round Saturday market under a brick riverside canopy where upstate farms sell cheese, cider and mushrooms and the knife sharpener works the crowd.
buzz: Locals say it is the best market in the capital region; get there by nine for the bread and stay for lunch from a stand.

name: Oakwood Cemetery
unique: A Victorian rural cemetery on a bluff above the Hudson holding Samuel Wilson, the meat packer behind Uncle Sam, along with Civil War generals and Tiffany windows in the chapel.
buzz: The Uncle Sam grave is the photo everyone takes; the self guided map at the gate points to the Earl Chapel, which is the real monument.

name: Saratoga Race Course
customer: Racing fans, groups, families on a picnic
unique: The oldest organized sporting venue in the country, where you can bring a cooler into the grandstand apron and watch the horses come down the stretch under the same 1860s trees.
buzz: The backyard picnic area is the local move; parking is a walk, the dress code is only in the clubhouse, and Travers week is chaos.

name: Saratoga Spa Mineral Springs
unique: A state park built around mineral springs where you can fill a bottle at a pavilion with water that tastes of iron and eggs, then take a carbonated bath in the 1935 Roosevelt Baths.
buzz: The taste is the story and everybody warns you; the Roosevelt Baths need booking and the park pools are the family alternative.

name: Saratoga Performing Arts Center
unique: An amphitheater in a state park where the New York City Ballet and Philadelphia Orchestra spend the summer and the lawn seats cost less than a city parking garage.
buzz: The lawn is the experience, with people carrying in full dinners and candles; the sound is better under the shell but the atmosphere is outside.
